newsitem.title: INDIA: India gilt prices further up, realign on new bond.
newsitem.headline: India gilt prices further up, realign on new bond.

text.p: Indian government security prices were sharply up in mid-morning trade as bonds were repriced following Wednesday's lower then expected yield on a new stock, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday set a 11.83 percent cut-off yield at an auction of six-year bonds against market expectations of 11.90-11.95 percent.
In latest deals, the 11.83 percent 2003 bond, auctioned at par on Wednesday, traded at 101.30 rupees, dealers said.

Other stocks which moved up were the 12.59 percent 2004 at 104.10 against its last traded 102.90, the 12.14 percent 2000 at 103.95 against 103.40 and the 13.85 percent 2000 at 108.45 against 107.92, dealers said.
The 12.50 percent 2004 traded at 103.80 against 102.75, they said.
"Prices are realigning on the new bond," said a dealer. "Prices are up, in some cases by more than a rupee, but the rise only reflects a repricing based on the new bond."
Another reason for the rise in prices was surplus liquidity with banks, he said.
At Wednesday's six-year bond auction, the RBI received bids for 130.45 billion rupees against a notified amount of 30 billion.

"This is a good sign of the excess funds with banks," the dealer said. "Call money rates have been below 2.0 percent for nearly a fortnight now and with corporate demand for credit at a low level, banks are looking to deploy their surplus funds in securities."
